title: Regional failover: missing timeseries and trace correlation gaps in Console
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary:
A multi-customer incident was triggered during a regional failover window where console dashboards stopped showing recent timeseries for several core metrics (request_rate, host_gpu_util, kv_cache_hit) and trace links in traces view were missing correlation ids for requests routed through Private deployments. Affected customers included three Hosted customers and two Dedicated customers; one Enterprise Private customer reported paying-production errors.

Scope & Systems:
- Metric ingestion pipeline (Kafka->metric-ingest->TSDB) experienced a partition rebalance that caused ~5-12 minute ingestion gaps for specific topic partitions.
- Grafana/Console dashboard queries were written to rely on metric label 'cluster_region' which was temporarily renamed to 'region_id' by an upstream transform during a schema migration. Panels depending on cluster_region returned empty time series.
- Tracing service: Private agent rollout introduced a small env var naming mismatch that dropped the 'x-rd-correlation-id' header when forwarding to the tracing collector, so traces lacked links back to request logs for Private customers.

Impact:
- Missing panels and flatlined graphs in Console led to five incoming escalations; two customers opened support tickets marked P1. One on-call alerted SRE; customers reported inability to confirm SLA compliance during the failover.

Root cause hypothesis: combination of transient ingestion backlog (Kafka rebalance) + dashboard query fragility to label-name churn + private agent config mismatch.

Goals for this ticket:
1) Implement immediate hotfixes to restore dashboards and trace linking for affected customers.
2) Add guardrails to metric pipeline to prevent partition rebalance-induced gaps and to alert proactively.
3) Harden dashboard queries to be resilient to label migrations and add fallback queries.
4) Update Private agent config validation and add e2e test that verifies correlation header propagation.

Planned deliverables:
- Hotfix PR to metric-ingest to add consumer-group checkpointing and graceful pause on rebalance (ENG-9450-1).
- Dashboard patch to use coalesced label selectors (region_id OR cluster_region) + added synthetic check panels (ENG-9450-2).
- Private agent release v2.8.3 with env var fix and new integration test; rolling update plan for Private customers.
- Post-incident runbook entry and SLA customer communication template.
comments: 2026-03-10 09:15 - Asha Patel: Incident opened after customer 'AtlasPay' reported empty latency and request_rate panels following the scheduled region failover. Initial triage assigned to SRE and Observability. Notified on-call SRE: Priya Rao.

2026-03-10 09:42 - Priya Rao: Observed Kafka consumer group saw a rebalance during failover; ingestion lag spiked to ~11 minutes for topic 'metrics.events.p1' on partition 7. Created temporary consumer restart play to flush backlog. See runbook link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/obs/incidents/ENG-9450

2026-03-10 10:20 - Liam O'Connor: Confirmed Grafana panels failing because dashboard queries filter on label 'cluster_region' which upstream transform renamed to 'region_id' in migration #MIG-2026-03. Rolling dashboard patch to use 'coalesce(region_id, cluster_region)' style query where supported. Draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/5241

2026-03-10 11:05 - Maya Chen (Customer Success): Customer-facing update sent: acknowledging issue, ETA for mitigation 2-4 hours, included temporary workaround to view raw series in Metrics Explorer. Ticket: CS-1922

2026-03-10 13:30 - Liam O'Connor: Hotfix deployed to metric-ingest: added rebalance handler to pause commits, drain buffers, and resume; consumer group checkpoint restored. Lag returned to normal within 6 minutes. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/metric-ingest/pull/211

2026-03-10 15:10 - QA: Validated dashboard patch locally across query engine versions; added fallback queries for 'region_id' and 'cluster_region'. Merged console PR and deploy to canary. Console PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/5241

2026-03-11 08:50 - SRE: Private agent issue reproduced in lab: env var RD_CORR_ID was used by agent v2.8.2 while tracing collector expects X_RD_CORR. Agent line-drop occurred when header key mismatch triggered filter. Hotfix agent release prepared (v2.8.3) and test added. Agent PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/private-agent/pull/88

2026-03-11 12:00 - Liam O'Connor: Began rolling update for Dedicated pools with updated metric-ingest config and console canary. Monitored with synthetic check. Dedicated customers report restored graphs.
2026-03-12 09:30 - Customer Success (Maya Chen): AtlasPay confirmed dashboards are now showing expected timeseries; they validated SLO windows. Case closed with follow-up survey pending.

2026-03-12 16:45 - Asha Patel: Post-mortem notes drafted. Action items included below. Planning follow-up EPIC for durable fixes and automation. Assigned owners for each action item. Link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/obs/postmortems/ENG-9450

2026-03-13 10:00 - Liam O'Connor: Added new synthetic monitors to detect label schema drift (alerts when >1% of series missing or when 'coalesce' fallback triggers). Also added a dashboard QA job to run against canary after every migration.
next_steps: 1) Complete agent e2e tests and promote v2.8.3 to Private customer upgrades (owner: Maya Chen). 2) Implement consumer-group shard monitoring + alerting to detect rebalance-induced lags (owner: Priya Rao). 3) Roll out dashboard coalescing changes across all templates and add CI regression to catch label renames (owner: Liam O'Connor). 4) Publish post-incident report and customer communication package (owner: Asha Patel).
